name: Chapin, Chiquita and Ypsilon (Mummy Range)
region: Rocky Mountain National Park, Mummy Range

legs.connect: Drop north from Chapin to the saddle in under 15 minutes, then follow the open ridge up about 1,000 ft to the Chiquita summit.
Return to the Chapin–Chiquita saddle area, then head north-northwest to the next saddle and climb the slope to Ypsilon.
Optional extension: continue along the ridge beyond Ypsilon; the ridge is loose and needs hands in places, so many parties drop onto the face instead.

how: All three main summits come from one trailhead at the pass, so doing them together is the normal outing. Go in order from the lowest, Chapin, to Chiquita and finally Ypsilon, the highest. The ridge walking is mostly easy class 2 on open tundra and scree. Adding Fairchild turns it into a harder class 3 outing with a loose, rough ridge between Ypsilon and Fairchild.
descent: Retrace the ridge back over the saddles and cut across the western slopes to the trailhead. With Fairchild added, many parties instead finish at a second trailhead and need a car shuttle.
logistics: Start at the trailhead just below the pass, well before dawn, since the whole outing is above treeline with weather exposure. A park entry fee or timed-entry rule may apply in season; the three-peak version takes roughly nine hours round trip.
notes: Three-peak combo listed as class 2, 9 mi, 3,750 ft gain; with Fairchild class 3, 11 mi, 5,150 ft (used higher class). Longer Mummy Mania traverse (Mummy, Hagues too) not verified from a second independent page, left out.

name: Gladstone Peak and Wilson Peak

legs.connect: Follow the ridge from Gladstone toward the saddle below Wilson, then climb Wilson's class 3 final section. Some parties drop into the basin and cross boulders to the saddle to avoid ridge difficulties.

how: Climbers start from the Rock of Ages side, reach the saddle, and go up Gladstone's north ridge first, then traverse over to Wilson Peak and return via the saddle. The ridge is mostly solid class 3 with a few optional class 4 moves, and the traverse takes about two hours. Wilson's own summit pitch is class 3 and adds the exposure of the link. Some parties also add an unnamed 13er beyond Wilson.
descent: Return to the Rock of Ages saddle from Wilson and walk back down the approach trail to the trailhead, rather than reversing the ridge.
logistics: Typical round trip is about 12 to 13 miles and over 5,000 ft of gain. Start early because the ridge is exposed and holds loose blocks; best in the dry summer and early fall window.
notes: The ridge from Gladstone to Wilson is rated class 4 on the route listing but class 3 in a 13er guidebook; class 4 is the cautious reading. Only two 2020 reports read.

name: Fletcher Mountain and Drift Peak

legs.connect: Descend the ridge from Fletcher to the saddle, then follow the ridge up to Drift, with a short loose steep notch downclimb and a loose class 3 climb back to the crest on the return.

how: Both summits are reached from the Blue Lakes basin south of Quandary. Fletcher is an easy rock pile and ridge; the extra reward of the link is Drift, joined by a ridge with a few class 3 sections and one short, steep, loose notch. Many parties tag them together because the saddle between them is a short walk. Some carry on to Quandary or Wheeler for a larger loop, but those extensions are harder or longer.
descent: Reverse the ridge, downclimb the loose section, then pick a line down to the tundra and drop through snowfields or scree back to the trailhead along the same approach.
logistics: Snow lingers in the basins into summer, so an axe may be useful early in the season. A longer loop continuing over Wheeler and North Star needs a car shuttle at the pass.
notes: A route listing reports class 3, about 5.5 mi, 2,800 ft gain for the pair (search snippet only, not read). The Quandary-Fletcher-Drift-Wheeler-North Star loop was read in one report only.
